\chapter{Hablasteis --- The Form You Were Promised}
\label{ch:hablasteis}
\hlchaptermodality{241}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can use every person of the -ar preterite.}

I can use every person of the -ar preterite.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[hablasteis]{hablasteis — the form you were promised}

\label{lesson:ES-C63-hablasteis}



\begin{quote}
The \emph{-ar} past, as far as you have it: \emph{hablé}, \emph{hablaste}, \emph{habló}, \emph{hablamos}, \emph{hablaron}.

Five of six. The review that closed the preterite told you the sixth was still owed. Here it is.
\end{quote}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: -steis}]
\begin{quote}
\emph{vosotros} \emph{\textbf{hablasteis}} — you all spoke
\end{quote}

Look at it beside the \emph{you} form you already know:

\noindent
\begin{tabularx}{\linewidth}{@{}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}X@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{} & \textbf{} \\
\midrule
\emph{tú} & \emph{habla} \emph{\textbf{ste}} \\
\emph{vosotros} & \emph{habla} \emph{\textbf{steis}} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}

The same \emph{-ste}, with \emph{-is} stacked on the end. That \emph{-is} is the plural marker you met back in the present, in \emph{habláis}. Nothing here is new; it is two pieces you own, in a row.
\end{grammarlens}

\begin{culture}
And with that, the \emph{-ar} preterite is \textbf{complete}:

\emph{hablé · hablaste · habló · hablamos · hablasteis · hablaron}

Six forms, no gaps. It is the first tense in this book you can say straight through without a promissory note at the end.

As with every \emph{vosotros} form, you will hear it in Spain and rarely elsewhere — but you will \textbf{read} it everywhere, which is reason enough to know it on sight.
\end{culture}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{hablaste}, then \emph{hablasteis}
  \item all six, straight through
\end{itemize}

\emph{Twice through:}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What is stacked on \emph{-ste} to make \emph{-steis}? (The plural \emph{\textbf{-is}}.)

And how many gaps are left in the \emph{-ar} past? (\textbf{None.})
\end{tcolorbox}
